scope: Independent focused technical assessment of native executable-path compatibility and launcher; not the Standards/Spec axes and not formal project acceptance.
outcome: No concrete kernel-integrity or launcher-boundary blocker found within the documented stable absolute-ELF launch contract.
assessment: The library first calls the actual SYS_readlink. It only synthesizes a result after ENOENT and exact matching of its own numeric-PID exe path or /proc/self/exe. Other paths and other errors return their actual syscall result; the prior errno is restored on fallback failure.

The fallback uses the process auxiliary vector AT_EXECFN, requires an absolute path, canonicalizes it, verifies readable ELF magic, and implements truncation without adding a NUL. It does not read another process, create proc entries, or alter host privileges or isolation.

The adapter checks exact source, compatibility-library, official Lean and official Lake digests; rejects unexpected preexisting LD_PRELOAD or LD_AUDIT; resolves its initial command to an absolute path; and applies the compatibility environment only to that command and descendants.

Recorded native Lake child-path and normal check.sh-entrypoint tests exercise the actual launch routes. Relative-ELF and interpreted-script probes correctly receive no synthetic result. Explicit dynamic-loader launches and replaced/deleted executables are outside the documented stable-path contract.

The additional loader library is a disclosed runtime trust component. Its sole exported global function is readlink; source and symbol evidence show no theorem-checking, axiom-audit, serialization, compiler-identity, or exit-result interception. Identical small-proof outputs support the setup but are not a proof of whole-program equivalence or chapter acceptance.

pinned_thread_behavior.compiled_runtime: runtime/object.cpp get_lean_num_threads reads LEAN_NUM_THREADS for lean_init_task_manager; this affects compiled tools such as Lake.
pinned_thread_behavior.lean_cli: Lean/Shell.lean defaultNumThreads uses hardware concurrency; mkShellOptions supplies that default; util/shell.cpp constructs scoped_task_manager from the parsed shell option. Lean CLI selects its task-manager worker count through supported -j/--threads, not this environment variable.
pinned_thread_behavior.lake_spawn: Lake.Build.Module.buildLean passes configured weakLeanArgs plus leanArgs; compileLeanModule adds outputs/setup/JSON arguments and overrides LEAN_PATH. No automatic -j argument or independent Lake --jobs option is present in the pinned path.
pinned_thread_behavior.qualification: LEAN_NUM_THREADS is not a hard global child-process cap. The r1/r2 cache result compares differing Lake runtime settings and does not establish four compiler workers versus one, or prove the cause of the QEMU stall.

operational_observation.note: Concrete remaining disk-space consideration before large project output generation, especially given retained ENOSPC history. This is not a native compatibility correctness finding.

mutations_during_assessment: Only this assessment record was created. No environment/source/cache/adapter edits, compiler invocation, or repeated tests.
